palettePlaceholder: Type the name of a command
keysConflict: A key runs more than one action
generalNote: What the window starts with, how its tabs behave, and what it asks before it closes.
interactionNote: How the terminal answers the mouse and the clipboard, and how much it keeps.
appearanceNote: How the window and the terminals look: the face of the window, the typesetting, the cursor, and the colors, over a preview that follows every change.
schemesNote: The colors the terminals paint with, and the schemes the settings keep.
actionsNote: What the window does, the keys it does it on, and which keys the file binds.
advancedNote: Probe the shells, open the folders the settings live in, or start over from the defaults.
defaultsNote: The settings a profile starts from, and the profiles this machine has.
defaultProfileNote: The profile a new tab runs unless it picks one; with none picked a new tab runs this machine's own shell.
startDirectoryNote: Where a new tab starts when its profile names no directory: current (where wt-go was started), home, or a path. Empty means home.
closeOnLastTabNote: Close the window when its last tab closes.
confirmCloseWindowNote: Ask before the window closes with more than one tab.
copyOnSelectNote: Copy what a selection takes as it takes it.
scrollMultiplierNote: How far a notch of the wheel and a touchpad's scrolling go; 1 scrolls the way the system's own setting does.
clipboardReadNote: What a program gets when it asks for the clipboard. Refused unless allowed here: a program that can read it sees what you copied elsewhere. Applies to new tabs.
clipboardWriteNote: Whether a program may put text on the clipboard. Applies to new tabs.
pasteMultilineNote: Ask before a paste that holds more than one line.
confirmCloseNote: Ask before a tab closes while its program still runs.
panesPerTabNote: How many panes a tab splits into; 0 for no limit.
themeNote: The face of the window: the system's, light, dark, or a theme of its own.
backgroundOpacityNote: How much of what is behind the window shows through it.
alwaysOnTopNote: Keep the window above the others.
titleFollowsPaneNote: Name the window after the pane with the keyboard.
colorSchemeNote: The colors a terminal paints with unless its profile names another. A scheme the settings keep says its colors in settings.json, which this page does not edit.
schemeCopied: The scheme is copied; save to keep it.
schemeRemoved: The scheme is removed; save to keep it.
fontNote: The monospaced families this machine has, as the terminal measures them. The first choice is the generic name every system resolves to one.
fontSizeNote: How tall the letters of a terminal are, in DIPs.
lineHeightNote: The height of a line of a terminal, as a multiple of the font size.
cursorNote: The shape the cursor has, and whether it blinks.
paddingNote: The space inside the edges of a terminal, in DIPs.
paddingColorNote: What the room around the text shows: the window's background, the cells nearest to it, so that a program that paints its own background reaches the edges, or always them. Applies to new tabs.
minimumContrastNote: The least contrast text has with its background, from 0 to 21: 0 draws every cell as the program wrote it, 4.5 is what the guidelines call readable.
scrollbackNote: How much a terminal keeps to scroll back through, in MB.
name: Name
commandLineNote: The program the profile runs; empty runs the shell the system starts.
discoveredProfileNote: The shell the window found on this machine; its path is not edited here.
commandEmptyHint: Empty: this profile runs the shell the system starts. To run a program of your own, type its path, such as {hint}.
argumentsNote: The arguments of the command, one on each line.
profileStartNote: Where the profile starts: current, home, a path, or empty to use the setting above.
iconNote: The mark the tab wears: one of the built-in shapes, or one character of your own (an emoji works). A shape paints its own colors, so the color below only holds for the other two.
iconColorNote: The color of the mark, for a profile that wears no shape: the plain terminal mark, or your character, in this color.
hiddenNote: Leave the profile out of the menu that opens tabs.
resetProfileDone: Gave {name} the program, the name and the color this machine has now.
resetProfileGone: This machine no longer has the program {name} runs, so the profile is hidden.
probeAgainNote: The window probes this machine when it writes its first settings file. Probing again gives every built-in profile the command that is installed now, hides the ones whose program is gone and shows the ones that are back. Names, colors and directories stay.
deleteSettingsNote: Deletes the file and starts the window again, which writes the defaults and probes the machine the way the first start did.
settingsFolderNote: Where settings.json lives. The file itself needs a program the desktop edits JSON with, which not every Linux desktop has, so the window opens the folder.
confirmProbeText: Every built-in profile takes the command the probe finds, one whose program is gone is hidden, and one that is there is shown again. Names, colors and directories stay.
confirmDeleteText: The window starts over with the defaults: fonts, colors, keybindings and profiles are all lost.
confirmPasteText: {count, plural, one {This pastes # line into the pane.} other {This pastes # lines into the pane.}}
confirmCloseSettingsText: The settings hold changes you have not saved.
confirmCloseWindowText: Closing the window closes all {count} tabs at once.
tabRunningText: The program in this tab is still running.
tabUnsureText: wt-go cannot tell whether this tab still runs a program.
tabAlwaysText: Closing the tab ends the shell it runs.
othersRunningText: Programs in the other tabs are still running.
othersUnsureText: wt-go cannot tell whether the other tabs still run programs.
othersAlwaysText: Closing the other tabs ends the shells they run.
probedNote: The shells are probed again; the file is written.
probeSameNote: The shells are what the file already says.
errRelaunch: The window could not start again: {error}
errOpenFolder: The folder could not be opened: {error}
errOpenLink: The link could not be opened: {error}
errOpenFile: The settings file could not be opened: {error}
settingsChangedNote: settings.json changed on disk; discard your changes to take it.
saveRefusedNote: Not saved: correct what is wrong and save again, or discard your changes.
errSettingsInvalid: settings.json is not valid: {error}; the original was kept at {path}
errSettingsInvalidKeep: settings.json is not valid: {error}; the original could not be kept: {keepError}
